paragraphs.title: Opening and the Rescue of Desert Travelers

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “O give thanks unto the LORD.”
easy.q: Whom does the psalm call to give thanks?

easy.explanation: They were gathered from the east, west, north, and south.
easy.q: From where were the redeemed gathered?

easy.explanation: They wandered in the wilderness and were hungry and thirsty.
easy.q: What was the condition of the travelers in the wilderness?

medium.explanation: They cried unto the LORD in their trouble.
medium.q: What did the travelers do in their trouble?

answers: He sent them back into the wilderness
He led them by the right way to a city of habitation
medium.explanation: He led them forth by the right way to a city of habitation.
medium.q: What did the LORD do after they cried unto Him?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the lonely, desolate wilderness.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “a solitary way” describe?

answers: Trouble immediately causes them to build a city
They cry out of their trouble, and the LORD delivers and guides them
They remain in trouble despite crying out
challenge.explanation: The passage presents trouble, crying out, deliverance, and guidance in sequence.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between trouble and deliverance?

answers: Arrival at an inhabited city and satisfaction of the hungry soul
challenge.explanation: The LORD leads them to a city and fills the hungry soul with goodness.
challenge.q: What result of the LORD’s deliverance is emphasized?

answers: The LORD’s mercy brings deliverance and calls forth thanksgiving
challenge.explanation: The passage calls people to praise the LORD for His goodness and wonderful works.
challenge.q: What repeated idea appears at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: In darkness and the shadow of death
easy.explanation: The KJV describes them as sitting in darkness and the shadow of death.
They were bound in affliction and iron.
They cried unto the LORD, and He saved them.
easy.q: What did the prisoners do in their trouble?

answers: They rebelled against God’s words and contemned His counsel
They could not find water in the wilderness
medium.explanation: They suffered because they rebelled against the words of God and rejected the counsel of the Most High.
medium.q: What was one reason given for the prisoners’ suffering?

answers: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death
He placed them in another prison
He sent them back into the wilderness
medium.explanation: He brought them out of darkness and broke their bands apart.
medium.q: What did the LORD do after the prisoners cried out?

medium.explanation: “Bands” refers to the restraints that bound them.
medium.q: What does “their bands” mean in this passage?

answers: Darkness and bonds contrasted with freedom and release
challenge.explanation: The prisoners move from darkness and bondage into freedom.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the passage?

answers: Gates of brass and bars of iron
challenge.explanation: The LORD broke the gates of brass and cut the bars of iron apart.
challenge.q: What barriers are broken in the description of deliverance?

answers: Crying out leads the LORD to save them and break their bonds
There is no connection between crying out and deliverance
challenge.explanation: The sequence is crying out, salvation, release from darkness, and broken bonds.
challenge.q: How does the passage connect crying out with freedom?

answers: They drew near to the gates of death
easy.explanation: The passage says that they drew near unto the gates of death.
easy.q: How serious was the condition of the afflicted?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Their soul abhorreth all manner of meat.”

answers: He left them in their affliction
easy.explanation: He sent His word, healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.
easy.q: What did the LORD do for them?

answers: The absence of an inhabited city
medium.explanation: The passage says they were afflicted because of their transgression and iniquities.
medium.q: What is described as a cause of their affliction?

answers: They cried unto the LORD in their trouble
medium.explanation: They cried unto the LORD, and He saved them from their distresses.
medium.q: What did the afflicted do before they were saved?

medium.explanation: The word refers to destructive or deadly conditions from which the LORD delivered them.
medium.q: In this context, what does “their destructions” refer to?

answers: Affliction, crying out, healing, and thanksgiving
challenge.explanation: The afflicted suffer, cry out, are healed, and offer thanksgiving.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of events in the passage?

answers: By offering sacrifices of thanksgiving and declaring the LORD’s works with rejoicing
challenge.explanation: They sacrifice sacrifices of thanksgiving and declare His works with rejoicing.
challenge.q: How do the rescued people express their thanks?

answers: Deliverance should end in recognition and thanksgiving
The rescued return to their sins
challenge.explanation: The repeated call connects healing and deliverance with praise for the LORD’s goodness.
challenge.q: What does the repeated call to praise the LORD emphasize?

answers: Those who do business in great waters
easy.explanation: The passage describes people who go down to the sea in ships to do business in great waters.
easy.q: Who go down to the sea in ships?

answers: The works of the LORD and His wonders
easy.explanation: They saw the works of the LORD and His wonders in the deep.
easy.q: What did the seafarers see in the deep?

answers: It caused them to build a city
easy.explanation: The LORD made the storm a calm, and the waves were still.
easy.q: What happened to the storm after the seafarers cried out?

answers: They reeled and staggered like a drunken man
medium.explanation: They reeled to and fro and staggered like a drunken man.
medium.q: How did the storm affect the seafarers?

medium.explanation: They cried unto the LORD, who brought them out of their distresses.
medium.q: What did the seafarers do in their trouble?

medium.explanation: “The deep” refers to the depths of the sea.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “the deep” refer to?

answers: They move from storm and fear to calm and their desired haven
They move from calm into prison
They move from hunger into the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The storm becomes calm, they rejoice, and the LORD brings them to their desired haven.
challenge.q: What change occurs in the seafarers’ condition?

challenge.explanation: They exalt Him in the congregation and praise Him among the elders.
challenge.q: What do they do after reaching safety?

answers: The LORD controls both the raising and calming of the storm
challenge.explanation: The passage attributes both the storm and its calming to the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the storm and the calm teach?

paragraphs.title: Changes in the World and the Establishment of Settlements

easy.explanation: The passage says, “He turneth rivers into a wilderness.”
easy.q: What can the LORD turn rivers into?

easy.explanation: The hungry prepared a city for habitation.
easy.q: What did the hungry establish where they dwelt?

easy.explanation: They sowed fields and planted vineyards.

answers: Turning the wilderness into standing water
Turning a city into a prison
medium.explanation: The LORD can turn the wilderness into standing water and dry ground into watersprings.
medium.q: What opposite transformation is described alongside turning rivers into a wilderness?

answers: They multiplied greatly, and their cattle did not decrease
medium.explanation: The LORD multiplied them greatly and did not allow their cattle to decrease.
medium.q: What happened after the LORD blessed the settlers?

answers: A condition of being unfruitful or desolate
medium.explanation: “Barrenness” describes land that is unproductive or desolate.
medium.q: What does “barrenness” mean in this passage?

challenge.explanation: The passage says people can be diminished and brought low through oppression, affliction, and sorrow.
challenge.q: What can reverse a process of growth and prosperity?

answers: The princes wander in a wilderness, while the poor are set on high and made into families
challenge.explanation: The LORD pours contempt upon princes but lifts the poor from affliction and gives them families.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between princes and the poor?

answers: The land and its inhabitants can change between abundance, desolation, and distress
The land has no connection with the condition of its inhabitants
challenge.explanation: The passage describes changes in the land and its people according to blessing, wickedness, and hardship.
challenge.q: What central idea emerges from these transformations?

paragraphs.title: Conclusion: The Joy of the Upright and Reflection on Kindness

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The righteous shall see it, and rejoice.”
easy.q: Who see these things and rejoice?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “all iniquity shall stop her mouth.”
The final verse begins, “Whoso is wise.”
easy.q: To whom does the final verse speak?

answers: These things and the lovingkindness of the LORD
Only the power of the storm
medium.explanation: The wise are called to observe these things and understand the LORD’s lovingkindness.

answers: The righteous see and rejoice, while the wise are called to understand the LORD’s lovingkindness
The wise are told to forget the deliverance
medium.explanation: The conclusion joins seeing, rejoicing, observing, and understanding.
medium.q: How are the joy of the righteous and the final verse connected?

medium.explanation: The expression pictures iniquity as being silenced.
medium.q: What does “stop her mouth” mean when used of iniquity?

answers: It calls people to see, rejoice, and understand the LORD’s lovingkindness
It focuses only on building ships
challenge.explanation: The conclusion turns the psalm’s events into a call to reflection and praise.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion summarize the psalm’s stories of deliverance and change?

answers: Righteousness is vindicated, while wickedness loses its voice
Iniquity becomes stronger than the righteous
There is no difference between the righteous and the wicked
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts the joy of the righteous with the silencing of iniquity.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the righteous rejoicing while iniquity is silenced?

answers: To observe these things and understand the lovingkindness of the LORD
challenge.explanation: The wise person is called to observe the psalm’s works and understand the LORD’s lovingkindness.
challenge.q: What role does wisdom have in the final verse?
